penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Providing actual GCP technical support requires domain-expert human engineers to diagnose infrastructure issues, read logs, and resolve blockers — Claude cannot reliably substitute for a GCP-certified engineer on production incidents.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Technical support engagements — especially for blocking production issues — require real-time or near-real-time back-and-forth, screenshares, or ticket triage by a human who understands the environment.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Each customer engagement is inherently a high-judgment, context-heavy interaction; support load scales linearly with customers and cannot be meaningfully automated away.

rationale: The target buyer is real and identifiable — SMB engineering leads and solo developers running production workloads on GCP who have actively tried to purchase support and been refused — and the willingness to pay is clearly demonstrated by that attempted purchase behaviour. However, the core delivery is bespoke, expert-level cloud infrastructure consulting, which requires a human GCP engineer per engagement; Claude cannot substitute here without creating serious quality and liability risk. The fatal constraint is operational_autonomy (scored 3): every customer ticket demands human expert judgement, synchronous communication, and per-case manual work, meaning this would function as a consulting practice rather than a productised micro-service.
solution_plan: This idea cannot realistically be built and maintained by a solo non-technical operator running an autonomous Claude factory. The core value — resolving blocking GCP infrastructure issues — requires a credentialed human cloud engineer to diagnose environments, interpret logs, and implement fixes. Even if intake and triage were automated via Claude, fulfilment is irreducibly manual and synchronous. A brokerage or reseller model (connecting buyers to GCP support partners) is structurally possible but thin-margin, requires maintaining a vetted engineer network, and still involves per-deal human coordination. This is a consulting/staffing play, not a micro-SaaS. Recommend dropping unless a narrow, fully-automatable sub-problem is identified (e.g. a self-serve GCP quota-increase guide, or an automated audit report) — but that would be a different opportunity.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy build gate (scored 3, floor is 7) and buildability_with_ai build gate (scored 4, floor is 6). Even at the validate stage the underlying business model is consulting-shaped, not product-shaped. The pain and buyer intent are genuine and high-quality; the problem is that autonomous delivery is not feasible. Total after penalties (2.3) falls well below the validate threshold (5.5), so the stage is drop.
